_comment: Ledger of claims that have been CORRECTED, and therefore must not survive anywhere.
This exists because a correction's scope is the CLAIM, not the file. On 2026-08-08 the
OrchidCLIP page was corrected to stop calling its holdout 'stratified' and to lead with
the per-genus average; the same two claims stayed live for a day in the orchid-clip
README and in the orchid-clip-v8 model card, where a reader clicking through from the
site would hit the retracted version. Nothing in CI could see that, because every
existing guard stops at the repository boundary.
retracted            strings that must appear on NONE of its surfaces
required             a string that MUST appear on at least one surface. This is the
positive control and is not optional: without it a fetch that
silently returns nothing reads as 'retracted text absent' and the
check passes while observing nothing at all.
surfaces             where this claim is published. A surface named here that the
crawler did not discover is a FAILURE, not a skip -- otherwise a
change to link markup quietly reduces coverage to zero.
allow_if_line_matches  regexes for lines where the old value legitimately appears,
i.e. a correction notice that quotes what it is correcting.

retractions.note: The page said records were pulled from 'GBIF, SERNEC, iDigBio and the Kent State herbarium'. The acquisition ledger contains zero Kent State URLs; the download was GBIF only. NOTE the ban strings are the CLAIM, not the entity: 'Kent State' alone appears truthfully in the repo README as the institution the undergraduate research was done at, advised by Dr. Andrea Case. Banning an entity name flags true statements about that entity.

The page volunteered that the 2024 measurements no longer exist on disk, and leaned on 'recovered' and 'survives' to explain the counts. That is a lab-notebook custody admission, not something a reader of an academic project page needs, and it reads badly to anyone assessing the work. The counts stand on their own.

The page quoted Christenhusz & Byng's ~28,000 accepted species while the pipeline itself dedups against WCVP, whose map here gives 30,581 accepted from 72,253 raw (GBIF backbone: 33,355). Quoting one authority while deduplicating against another is the defect; 28,000 was also the lowest of the three, so it understated the difficulty being described.

The page claimed the transgressive residual 'survives permutation testing and reproduces under a DINOv2 backbone, so it is not an artifact of the embedding'. The DINOv2 run is real, but both it and the v8 report carry verdict MARGINAL and genetics_pass false, and no permutation test or G1a off-chord output exists in stage15/16/17. What replicates is the CHORD, with numbers now on the page; the residual is graded marginal.
retracted: not an artifact of the embedding

retractions.note: Not a retraction but a cross-surface invariant, and the reason the pypi fetch path exists at all. The site and the plant-genomics-mcp PyPI description both state '50 tools across 23 backends', verified from source (Tool( appears exactly 50 times in server.py). The PyPI description is public and is never hyperlinked from the site, so nothing else can see it drift. An entry with no `retracted` list is legitimate: `required` alone pins a number that must agree everywhere it is published.

The holdout is md5(source_id) under --val-fraction 0.02; --cap-per-species, the balancing flag, defaults to 0. Calling it stratified claimed the one design choice that would have evened out the composition.

top1 in the harness is correct1/n, per image. Ophrys is 2,754 of 4,000 images and gains least (+2.8 pp), so the per-image mean is the statistic that hides the long tail the page argues for. Macro over the 14 reported genera is 0.768 -> 0.844, +7.6 pp.

Transcribing the intake ledger at a fixed row read '?' for the two tabs with a 7-row header and silently dropped them, giving 2,733 across 20 species. Reading by label gives 4,085 across 22 of 23 tabs. The repo README quotes the old figure inside its own correction notice, which is exactly right and must not trip this check -- hence allow_if_line_matches.
